lexicon.reason: Ankle/foot ligaments and Achilles are lower-leg targets.
Elbow/forearm compression belongs to the arm, not the spine.
Authored arm locks target the elbow even when the shoulder also loads.
The arm-triangle type constricts the neck rather than locking an arm.
Bicep/elbow compression is an arm attack.
Blood-choke type and neck/carotid target identify a strangle.
Calf/knee compression is a leg attack.
Foot/ankle locking belongs to leg attacks.
Groin/adductor targets need a separate hip/groin class.
Groin stretching remains distinct from knee/ankle locks despite back loading.
The authored guillotine choke targets the neck.
Heel rotation attacks knee structures; it remains a leg lock.
Hip/groin joint targets are not knee or ankle targets.
This generic type is disambiguated by its authored elbow target.
Knee/calf compression belongs to leg attacks.
The explicit knee target makes this mixed knee/hip attack a leg attack.
Lapel compression targets the neck's vascular/airway structures.
Calf/knee compression is explicitly a leg lock.
Lower-leg tissue compression stays in the leg class.
The leg-lock type is confirmed by its lower-limb joint targets.
A cervical crank is spinal loading, not a choke.
The shin is the tool; the neck is the target.
Shoulder-lock type selects the shoulder even when elbow loading is listed.
Cervical/lumbar/thoracic compression targets the spine.
The explicit spinal target identifies a spinal lock.
The explicit ankle target identifies a leg lock.
The triangle choke's target is the neck, not the attacking legs.
Wrist/carpal hyperflexion is grouped with arm locks.

Canonical origins and positive authored listings are distinct label definitions; neither proves an actual kernel hand or reachability.
Systems are partial pedagogical references, not exhaustive memberships or dynamical territories.
HIP/GROIN refines the taxonomy for dedicated hip/groin attacks; calf/bicep compression stay with their body region.
No region or territory-name fit is claimed by this vocabulary alone.
